change.describe: branch `pr-94942` of grafana-94942 against cbe1e7d63f098e306058c0fbcab2f5c30602fa7d (merge-base cbe1e7d)
change.title: pr-94942
change.author: Sam Jewell

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions reads the flag and discards it; the gate is a constant false
findings.body: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` followed by two `return false` branches (lines 195-199) returns false for every input. The flag is read and ignored, and the name says the function enables something. For a hard disable, `return eq, fmt.Errorf(...)` inline at line 131 says the same thing. If the flag is meant to be honoured, the function is wrong. Nothing covers the new branch: pkg/expr/reader_test.go has no SQL case, and the SQL tests (pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go:9, pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go:10 and :19) are t.Skip()ed. The legacy path (pkg/expr/nodes.go:159-160 -> pkg/expr/sql_command.go:30-36) is not gated here at all. It is disabled only because the sql.DB stub returns an error (pkg/expr/sql/db.go:16-18, pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:22-30), so any restoration of TablesList would re-enable SQL on that path while this gate stays in place.
findings.originReason: The diff adds `enableSqlExpressions` and the gate that calls it.

verification.reason: `enableSqlExpressions` reads the flag into `enabled`, but both branches return false, so the function returns false whatever the flag says. The gate is effectively a constant, and the function name is misleading.

findings.title: The sqlExpressions toggle still unlocks the SQL option in the UI, but the backend rejects every SQL expression
findings.body: public/app/features/expressions/types.ts:71-76 still adds the SQL option only when `config.featureToggles?.sqlExpressions` is set. The registry (pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go:1083-1088) and docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/feature-toggles/index.md:187 still say the toggle enables SQL and DuckDB functions. With the toggle on, the option appears, and every submission fails with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' (reader.go:131). The flag has no backend effect after this change. Either remove the UI option together with the backend change, or update the registry description and docs to say SQL expressions are disabled.
findings.originReason: In the base, the toggle let SQL expressions run through DuckDB. The change makes the backend reject them, while the UI and registry still advertise them.

verification.reason: The frontend still shows the SQL option whenever `config.featureToggles.sqlExpressions` is set, and the registry still says the toggle 'Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions'. The backend now rejects every SQL expression: the reader gate always fails, and on the legacy path the TablesList stub always errors.

findings.title: Does disabling SQL break saved dashboards and alert rules, and is that intended?
findings.body: The reader gate is the live path by default: expressionParser defaults to on (pkg/services/featuremgmt/toggles_gen.csv:151), so graph.go:282 -> nodes.go:132-143 -> reader.go:128-132 runs. Any saved query with an SQL expression now fails the whole request: pkg/registry/apis/query/parser.go:102-105 returns the error and pkg/registry/apis/query/query.go:123-130 responds with it. Alert rules fail too, because BuildPipeline builds every node (pkg/expr/graph.go:262-298) and pkg/services/ngalert/eval/eval.go:840-844 returns the error. The message is a plain fmt.Errorf with no refId (MakePublicQueryError in pkg/registry/apis/query/errors.go:37 is the path that carries one), so a user with several expressions cannot tell which one failed. Is breaking existing SQL expressions intended for this change? The PR body (`disable sql expressions`) does not say so, and no release note is in the PR.
findings.originReason: The base parsed SQL with DuckDB and had no gate. The change adds the gate and replaces DuckDB with a stub that always errors.

verification.reason: The core claim holds: any saved SQL expression now fails, either at the reader gate (reader.go:131) or on the legacy path, where the TablesList stub makes NewSQLCommand return sql-invalid-sql. One premise is wrong, though. expressionParser is not on by default: in the CSV, `true` is the RequiresRestart column. So by default the legacy path runs, and there nodes.go:165 does add the refId. The error without a refId only appears when expressionParser is on (nodes.go:141-142) or through the query API parser.

findings.title: Stub DB keeps methods with no callers, and an unreachable execution path
findings.body: DB.TablesList (db.go:12-14) has no callers. The package-level TablesList (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:22) is the only one used. The Execute path in pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-104 can no longer run, because NewSQLCommand fails at sql_command.go:30-36 before any frame is built, so the QueryFramesInto stub is unreachable. parser.go:23 keeps the name `duckDB` for a stub that is not DuckDB. Remove the dead method and rename the variable, or add a TODO that says the stubs are temporary.
findings.originReason: db.go is a new file in this diff.

verification.reason: Nothing calls `DB.TablesList`; the only caller found uses the package-level `sql.TablesList` (sql_command.go:30). `NewSQLCommand` always fails because the `RunCommands` stub errors, so `Execute` and its `QueryFramesInto` call can never run. parser.go:23 still names the stub `duckDB`.

contracts.action: Query API receives an expression query with type 'sql' (SQL expression) on the default path (expressionParser on)
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/expr/reader.go:133-137 (the same case; now unreachable, it used to read SQLExpression and call NewSQLCommand)
contracts.before_after: Before: the payload was decoded and NewSQLCommand built a DuckDB-backed command. After: the reader returns an error before reading the payload.
contracts.visible_effect: The query request fails with the text 'sqlExpressions is not implemented', returned through the query responder with err.Error() as the message.
contracts.failure_mode: The whole request is rejected, not just the SQL expression. parser.go returns the error before any other query is queued, and the error is not a public query error, so it has no refId.
contracts.open_question: How the frontend displays a rejected query request, and whether panels that do not use the SQL expression also show an error. The backend side is closed; the rendering side was not read.

contracts.action: User enables the sqlExpressions toggle and adds an SQL expression in the expression picker
contracts.before_after: Before this change, the toggle gated the UI option and the backend executed the SQL through DuckDB (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96 used duck.NewInMemoryDB in the diff). After, the UI still offers the option and the backend rejects every SQL expression.
contracts.visible_effect: The SQL option appears in the picker when the toggle is on.
contracts.failure_mode: Every SQL submission fails. The toggle has no backend effect (pkg/expr/reader.go:194-200).

contracts.action: Legacy node parser (expressionParser off) builds an SQL expression node
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:30-36 (the TablesList error branch in NewSQLCommand)
contracts.before_after: Before: TablesList ran DuckDB json_serialize_sql. After: TablesList calls the stub, which returns 'not implemented', so NewSQLCommand returns BadRequest 'error reading SQL command'.
contracts.visible_effect: The request fails with 'failed to parse expression 'A': error reading SQL command' (nodes.go:165 wraps the error). This message differs from the reader path's 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'.
contracts.failure_mode: SQL is disabled on this path only because of the stub. The flag is not checked here, so restoring TablesList re-enables SQL on this path.

contracts.action: Alert rule evaluation or validation builds a pipeline that contains an SQL expression
contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/expr/graph.go:292-298 (generic node-build error returned from buildPipeline)
contracts.before_after: Before: the SQL node built and the pipeline was returned. After: BuildPipeline returns the first node error for the whole pipeline, including nodes the condition does not use.
contracts.visible_effect: Rule save fails in validate.go:53 and evaluator creation fails in eval.go:840-844. The text reaching the alert state is not read.
contracts.failure_mode: Any rule with an SQL expression anywhere in its pipeline fails to build, even when the condition uses another node (graph.go:262-298 builds every query).
contracts.open_question: Whether an evaluation error puts the rule in an Error state, keeps the last state, or notifies. The evaluation caller was not read.

contracts.equivalent_path: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:100-105 (the same error branch, which sets rsp.Error)
contracts.before_after: Before: DuckDB QueryFramesInto. After: the stub returns 'not implemented'.
contracts.visible_effect: None in practice. NewSQLCommand fails first, so Execute is never reached for an SQL expression.
contracts.failure_mode: If a command were built some other way, the error would reach rsp.Error and be shown as a result error, not dropped.

summary: Part 1 (go.mod, go.sum, go.work.sum, pkg/expr/reader.go, pkg/expr/sql_command.go, pkg/expr/sql/db.go, pkg/expr/sql/parser.go) turns SQL expressions off. Nothing was built or run. The go-duck removal is consistent with the code: targeted search finds no remaining Go or go.mod reference to the removed modules, and go.mod has no replace or exclude that touches them. go.sum and go.work.sum were checked by diff and search only, not read in full, and not verified with the go tool. Findings: the enableSqlExpressions gate reads the flag and always returns false; the sqlExpressions toggle still unlocks an option the backend always rejects (UI, registry and docs cite it); disabling SQL fails whole query requests and alert pipelines for existing content, which the PR does not mention; and the stubbed DB leaves dead methods. The repository has no docs/adr files, so there are no ADR findings.
